name: Texture-Enhanced Direct Volume Rendering
definition: A methodology for direct volume rendering that extends the standard color-opacity transfer function process by enabling the use of textures to encode additional information (e.g., fiber direction, cellular abnormalities) throughout the volume in three dimensions, rather than just on cutting planes.
summary: Texture-Enhanced Direct Volume Rendering encodes volumetric attributes as 3D textures for smooth, volume-wide transitions, unlike methods restricted to 2D planar slices.
